//emulators: The local suite the rules above are tested against (#267). Ports are pinned because www/shared/firebase.js hard-codes them: a page loaded as localhost:8123/word/?emu=1 talks to these two instead of the real project, which is the only way to try a rules change without deploying it to everyone first. Auth is here as well as database because every rule now reads auth.uid, and a page signed in against the real project hands the database emulator a uid it cannot verify. Needs a JDK 21 or newer: JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21 firebase emulators:start --only database,auth

hosting.//: predeploy regenerates www/ from src/, so a deploy can never ship stale HTML. Needs node_modules present: run npm ci if a deploy fails here.
hosting.//redirects: The dashboard is served at /admin and reached three other ways (#207). All 301, because none of the old spellings is coming back. Kept for the bookmark, not as a secret: the URL was never what protected the numbers, the rule on `analytics` is. shared/auth.js still excludes `stats` from account counting, so a stale bookmark cannot count a visit on its way through the redirect.
hosting.//rewrites: One clean URL, not site-wide `cleanUrls`. Every other page here is a directory index already served without an extension, so turning cleanUrls on would change how eight indexed pages resolve to buy nothing. This rewrites the one path that needs it, and leaves the rest of the site untouched. Redirects run before rewrites, so /admin.html 301s to /admin and this then serves the file: no loop.
